summary: the bigmem cases on x86-64, against a memory report that overstates the usable memory, a frame map that leaves out the memory past 4 GiB, and a frame allocator that never gives out a frame past 4 GiB

argv: ARCH=x86_64 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh make rach2 test-image && ARCH=x86_64 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh copy ${WORK} rach2/kernel

faults.name: usable-overstated
faults.summary: the memory report giving 4 KiB more usable memory than the map has, which the 8 GiB case finds against the map and against QEMU's size, and the 72 GiB case against the 63 GiB below 64 GiB

faults.name: unmapped-above-4g
faults.summary: the frame map clipped at 4 GiB, so that the memory past it is counted unreachable and never managed: the 8 GiB case finds it unreachable, memprobe 5120 runs out of frames, and the 72 GiB case counts 69 GiB unreachable

faults.name: frames-below-4g
faults.summary: a frame allocator whose scan above the window stops at 4 GiB, so that the frames past it are counted and managed but never given out, which memprobe 5120 finds when its pages run out of frames
